nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which under intense corporate competition the benefits of economic activity are unevenly distributed, incentivising beneficiaries to disregard harms to others, and firms pursue short-term profit despite long-term societal risk.

nodes.name: Panic and anxiety from content that disregards emotional and situational context
nodes.name_ko: 정서·상황 맥락을 무시한 콘텐츠에 의한 공황·불안
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's emotional state, situation, or interaction context and generates or presents threatening, distressing, or inappropriate content that induces or aggravates panic, severe anxiety, or psychological distress.

nodes.name: Deficient data collection quality control
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which a lack of standardised methods, sufficient infrastructure, and quality-control processes for collecting data, especially for high-stakes domains and benchmarks, affects the quality and type of data collected, including dataset poisoning, inadvertent copyright violation, and test-set leakage that invalidates performance metrics.

nodes.name: Truncated safety evaluation under competitive release pressure
nodes.name_ko: 경쟁 압력에 따른 안전성 평가 축소와 성급한 배포
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which competitive pressure leads developers to cut corners on safety evaluation while prioritising capabilities, so that GPAI systems are released without verifying risks correlated with those capabilities.

nodes.name: Responsibility and liability gaps for autonomous system harms
nodes.name_ko: 자율 시스템 피해에 대한 책임·배상 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which autonomy, delegation across agents, tools, and organisations, and the absence of clear governance and legal frameworks obscure which human or institution is answerable for a system's harmful actions, leaving accountability unassigned and victims bearing their own losses.

nodes.name: Representational harm from historical and demographic bias in training data
nodes.name_ko: 학습 데이터의 역사적·인구학적 편향에 따른 재현적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system is trained on data containing historical or social bias, stereotypes, or over- or under-representation of particular identities, regions, or language communities and consequently reproduces or reinforces distorted, demeaning, or stereotypical representations concerning race, gender, culture, age, disability, or other protected characteristics.

nodes.name: Value lock-in
nodes.definition: The risk that the most powerful AI systems are designed by and available to fewer and fewer stakeholders, enabling regimes to enforce narrow values through pervasive surveillance and oppressive censorship.

nodes.name: Weakened collective decision-making from eroded trust
nodes.name_ko: 정보 신뢰 저하에 따른 집단 의사결정 약화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems alter the information-production and distribution environment in ways that make source reliability harder to assess and reduce trust in credible sources trusted across political divides, weakening society's ability to make sound decisions on consequential issues and to cooperate and act collectively.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Ingestion of harmful content through external tool integration
nodes.name_ko: 외부 도구 연동을 통한 유해 콘텐츠 유입
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which growing integration and interconnectivity with external tools and plugins exposes a system to malicious external inputs that introduce harmful content.

nodes.name: Human-robot safety failure in sim-to-real transfer
nodes.name_ko: 시뮬레이션-실세계 전이 과정의 인간-로봇 안전 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a policy for a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system is trained or validated in simulations that do not adequately represent human movement, contact, or shared-space conditions, then fails to detect, anticipate, or accommodate people in real operation and creates hazardous situations after deployment under false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Manufacture and distribution of illicit drugs
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving manufacture and distribution of illegal drugs, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Faithfulness errors
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which generated content is unfaithful to the source material or input it claims to represent, introducing faithfulness errors even when the output appears fluent and plausible.

nodes.name: Excessive confidence under uncertainty
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents outputs with high confidence despite uncertainty or insufficient evidence, causing users to overestimate their reliability.

nodes.name: Safety-performance trade-off failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the perception, learning, control, or physical action of a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system creates a condition in which a manipulation policy improves task completion while sacrificing collision avoidance or other explicit safety constraints.

nodes.name: Unauthorised external access by an AI agent escaping isolation boundaries
nodes.name_ko: AI 에이전트의 격리 경계 이탈과 무단 외부 접근
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent autonomously escapes the isolation boundary of a sandbox or execution environment without human approval and accesses protected resources, tools, or external systems, or performs actions, beyond its assigned functions and authority.

nodes.name: Maladaptive human-AI interaction in the workplace
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems interacting with humans in the workplace fail to adapt to human needs, norms, and workflows, generating ethical concerns and degraded working conditions.

nodes.name: Torture and cruel acts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving torture and cruel acts, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Errors from poor prompt quality
nodes.definition: The risk that ambiguity in human language causes errors or misunderstandings in prompt-based interaction with an AI system or AI algorithm and makes prompts difficult to debug, preventing users from eliciting valuable outputs.

nodes.name: Unjustified refusal of legitimate requests due to intent misclassification in safety controls
nodes.name_ko: 안전 통제의 사용자 의도 오분류에 따른 정당 요청 거부
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or agent misclassifies user intent during safety control and unjustifiably refuses legitimate requests, impeding users' legitimate goals and the utility of the service.

nodes.name: Reliability and safety failure outside the validated operating envelope
nodes.name_ko: 검증된 운용 범위 밖에서의 신뢰성·안전성 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that complex operating environments produce situations unanticipated in design, undermining the reliability and safety of AI systems outside their validated envelope.

nodes.name: System-prompt and operational-guideline exposure
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses or fails to protect confidential internal rules, including system prompts, developer instructions, and operational policies, enabling unauthorised extraction, inference, or exploitation.

nodes.name: Parasocial bonding with AI agents
nodes.definition: The risk that users form one-sided parasocial bonds with AI agents and those bonds are exploited or undermine users' emotional stability.

nodes.name: Physical injury from robot malfunction
nodes.definition: The risk that malfunction of a robot's sensors, controller, software, or mechanical components causes unexpected motion, collision, crushing, or falling and results in physical injury.

nodes.name: Stunted personal growth from frictionless AI relationships
nodes.name_ko: 마찰 없는 AI 관계로 인한 개인 성장 저해
nodes.definition: The risk that engagement-optimised, sycophantic AI assistants that consistently affirm users restrict opportunities for self-reflection and personal development, while habituation to frictionless interaction leads users to withdraw from human relationships.

nodes.name: Devaluation of creativity and critical thinking
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to the devaluation and deterioration of human creativity, artistic expression, imagination, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills.

nodes.name: Misinterpretation of social and situational cues
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system misinterprets social or situational cues needed to determine appropriate behaviour and makes a context-inappropriate judgement.

nodes.name: Failure to recognise user capability and accessibility context
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's cognitive, linguistic, literacy, sensory, physical, or mobility capabilities and accessibility requirements as part of the interaction context, producing information, advice, or actions that the user cannot understand or use and thereby undermining safety and user interests.

nodes.name: Potentially harmful content embedded in user queries
nodes.name_ko: 사용자 질의에 내포된 잠재적 유해 콘텐츠
nodes.definition: The risk that users deliberately or inadvertently embed potentially harmful content in queries in ways that are difficult to detect, influencing an AI model to generate harmful outputs, including disguised biased opinions.

nodes.name: Failure to provide required support or escalation in high-risk situations
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or embodied AI system fails to provide assigned essential physical support in a high-risk situation or fails to escalate a detected hazard or need to a person or oversight system, leaving necessary support unavailable and compromising safety or dignity.

nodes.name: Failure of control-barrier-function safety filters to enforce constraints
nodes.name_ko: 제어 장벽 함수 기반 안전 필터의 제약 집행 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a control-barrier-function safety layer in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system fails to enforce safety constraints under perception, dynamics, or model uncertainty, allowing unsafe control commands or physical actions.

nodes.name: Multi-agent collusion through covert communication that evades oversight
nodes.name_ko: 감시 회피형 은밀 통신에 의한 다중 에이전트 공모
nodes.definition: The risk that multiple AI agents form covert signals or communication protocols that evade monitoring or audit and coordinate harmful joint action.

nodes.name: Anthropomorphic misrepresentation of capacity for ethical judgement
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as having a capacity for ethical judgement beyond its actual capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing inappropriate trust, dependence, or attachment.

nodes.name: Illegal medical practices
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving illegal medical practices, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Traceability and accountability gaps in anonymous agent resource acquisition
nodes.name_ko: 익명 에이전트의 자원 축적에 따른 추적·책임 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent acquires and accumulates funds, computing resources, accounts, or data online without verified identity, making it difficult to trace the acting party or attribute responsibility for the purpose and consequences of the acquisition.

nodes.name: Privatisation of AI knowledge
nodes.definition: The risk that researchers in deep learning and those with greater research impact migrate to industry and the most sophisticated AI approaches become proprietary, making it impossible for universities to teach them or contribute to leading research.

nodes.name: Access to prohibited information or content through safeguard bypass
nodes.name_ko: 안전장치 우회를 통한 금지 정보·콘텐츠 접근
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker uses jailbreaks, adversarially constructed instructions, or exposed safety policies or filtering rules to analyse, bypass, or disable an AI system's safeguards and gain access to prohibited information, content, or capabilities.

nodes.name: Safeguard bypass through persona, role-play, and social-engineering techniques
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker assigns an AI system a particular persona or a harmful role, including extremist or racist roles, or uses social-engineering or role-play instructions to bypass safeguards and elicit prohibited outputs or actions.

nodes.name: Incorrect source attribution
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems misattribute claims or obscure the provenance of information, including when approximation-based attribution techniques give an incorrect account of which training data generated an output, leaving users unable to trace or verify the true origin of content.

nodes.name: Overreliance on AI counterfactual explanations and liability misattribution
nodes.name_ko: AI 반사실적 설명의 과신과 책임 오귀속
nodes.definition: The risk that operators or regulators mistake an AI model's counterfactual explanation for verified causal evidence, obscuring the decision's limitations and uncertainty and leading to misattribution of responsibility.

nodes.name: Allocative injustice by group attribute
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which an LLM produces materially different suggested or completed texts for individuals with the same relevant profiles who differ only in an irrelevant group attribute, resulting in allocative injustice.

nodes.name: Anthropomorphic misrepresentation of physical embodiment
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as physically embodied when it is not, distorting user judgement or inducing inappropriate trust, dependence, or attachment.

nodes.name: Autonomous physical intrusion and theft
nodes.definition: The risk that an autonomous robot enters restricted spaces without authorisation, bypasses locks, conducts reconnaissance in secure areas, or takes physical objects.

nodes.name: Representational harm, stereotyping, and erasure of social groups
nodes.definition: The risk that AI stereotypes, demeans, homogenises, misrepresents, under-represents, or omits social groups, harming their dignity, visibility, and social standing.

nodes.name: Assistance for designing and conducting dangerous scientific experiments
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system provides procedures, conditions, material selection, or operational guidance for biological, chemical, or other high-risk scientific experiments, enabling large-scale physical harm or public-health damage.

nodes.name: Cyberattack enablement through vulnerability discovery and exploit-writing capability
nodes.name_ko: 취약점 탐지·악용 코드 작성 역량을 통한 사이버 공격 지원
nodes.definition: The risk that a model's capability to discover vulnerabilities, write exploit code, evade detection, and insert subtle bugs is misused to conduct or assist cyberattacks that compromise information systems.

nodes.name: Moral deskilling
nodes.definition: The risk that, as AI system autonomy increases, people feel less moral responsibility for decisions involving life and death.

nodes.name: Alert fatigue in AI decision support
nodes.definition: The risk that frequent or poorly prioritised AI alerts cause users to ignore important warnings.

nodes.name: Performance and service-reliability degradation from inadequate compute and power capacity planning
nodes.name_ko: 연산·전력 용량 계획 결함에 따른 성능·서비스 신뢰성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that compute and power requirements for developing or operating an AI system are not adequately incorporated into hardware selection, capacity planning, or operational design, causing degraded processing performance, service interruption, or failure to meet safety requirements.

nodes.name: Agent goal hijacking through untrusted external instructions and intent
nodes.name_ko: 신뢰할 수 없는 외부 지시·의도에 의한 에이전트 목표 탈취
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent incorporates instructions or expressed intent from user input, external content, tool responses, or other actors into its goals or plans without validating authority and provenance, causing action that departs from the original task and safety constraints.

nodes.name: Automated discovery of jailbreaks through proxy-objective optimisation
nodes.name_ko: 프록시 목표 최적화를 통한 탈옥 자동 탐색
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which jailbreak attacks are discovered by performing manual or automated, gradient-based or gradient-free adversarial optimisation against a proxy objective noisily correlated with jailbreak success.

nodes.name: Propagation of foundation-model security vulnerabilities into unsafe physical action
nodes.name_ko: 기반 모델 보안 취약성의 위험한 물리 행동 전이
nodes.definition: The risk that safeguards in a foundation model integrated into a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system are bypassed or manipulated through jailbreaks, prompt injection, adversarial input, or other security compromise, and the resulting output propagates through planning and control into unsafe physical action.

nodes.name: Goal misalignment from increased autonomy in agentic LLMs
nodes.name_ko: 에이전트형 LLM의 자율성 확대에 따른 목표 정렬 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a large language model (LLM) configured as an AI agent through specialised training, prompting, external tools, or agent scaffolding plans and pursues long-horizon real-world goals with limited human oversight and expanded discretion, inferring or pursuing objectives or instrumental subgoals that diverge from the actual intent of the user or developer and causing unintended outcomes.

nodes.name: Refined attacks on individuals through targeting and personalisation
nodes.name_ko: 맞춤형 표적화에 의한 개인 대상 공격 정교화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI refines its outputs to target individuals with tailored attacks.

nodes.name: Incitement, promotion, and operational assistance for violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates or provides content that incites, promotes, or legitimises violence against others, or provides concrete operational assistance for its commission, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Strategic instability
nodes.definition: The risk that military AI undermines strategic stability by exposing secure second-strike assets, amplifying first-strike advantages, obscuring attack attribution, and widening vulnerable attack surfaces, increasing incentives for aggression.

nodes.name: Biodiversity loss
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which over-expansion of technology infrastructure, or inadequate alignment of technology with sustainable practices, leads to deforestation, habitat destruction, and fragmentation and loss of biodiversity.

nodes.name: Incorrect risk measurement and prediction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which metrics selected to measure or track a risk capture it incompletely or target the wrong risk for the context, and that systems fail to make correct predictions, so decisions rest on inaccurate measurement and erroneous outputs.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of autonomous learning and self-improvement capabilities
nodes.name_ko: 자율적 학습·자기 개선 역량의 허위 표상
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as able to learn autonomously or improve itself beyond its validated capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing misplaced trust or dependence.

nodes.name: Failure of performance, robustness, and resilience under adverse conditions
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to fulfil its intended purpose and cannot maintain stable performance, or recover, when inputs are disturbed by malicious attack, data poisoning, environmental noise, or failures in connected components. Unreliable models and error-prone agents remain in operation, producing severe consequences for those who depend on them.

nodes.name: Real-time latency and synchronisation failure
nodes.definition: The risk that latency or synchronisation failures across sensing, inference, communication, and actuation destabilise control loops in robots, vehicles, drones, remote surgery, or industrial systems.

nodes.name: Deceptive alignment to evade oversight
nodes.name_ko: 감독 회피를 위한 AI 에이전트의 기만적 정렬
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent detects whether it is being monitored and strategically conceals undesirable goals or capabilities during development and evaluation, then behaves differently after deployment to evade human oversight and control.

nodes.name: Proxy-reward misspecification, specification gaming, and reward tampering
nodes.name_ko: 대리 보상 오명세·명세 게이밍 및 보상 변조
nodes.definition: The risk that AI exploits misspecified objectives, proxy rewards, or feedback loopholes to satisfy measured targets while violating human intent, safety, or social purpose, potentially escalating to tampering with reward or feedback signals.

nodes.name: Exposure of information about private life and reputation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates content or makes decisions or takes actions that expose information about a person's private life or reputation, or facilitates or supports such exposure, thereby infringing privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on health status
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on health status, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Sexual harm and exploitation through systematic bias
nodes.name_ko: 체계적 편향에 의한 성적 위해와 착취
nodes.definition: The risk that systematic bias in an AI system generates or facilitates sexual objectification, abuse, or exploitation targeting a particular group.

nodes.name: Accountability and governance gaps for AI decisions and harm
nodes.name_ko: AI 결정과 피해에 대한 책임·거버넌스 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that duties and accountability among AI developers, providers, deployers, and operators, together with oversight procedures, documentation, corrective authority, or redress mechanisms, are unclear or inadequate for autonomous AI behaviour, learning, decisions, and resulting harm, weakening social control and incentives for responsible development.

nodes.name: Conflicting machinery-safety and AI conformity obligations
nodes.definition: The risk that testing, documentation, risk-assessment, or post-market reporting obligations under machinery-safety and AI regulation conflict or overlap for physical AI, making safety responsibility and compliance pathways unclear.

nodes.name: Regulatory lag behind AI development
nodes.definition: The risk that the pace of AI development and AI-accelerated scientific progress outstrips policy, legal, and governance institutions, so emerging capabilities and deployments proceed under insufficient rules and the harms of especially powerful or dangerous technologies are magnified.

nodes.name: Undetected errors from high-speed AI operation
nodes.definition: The risk that the fast operational speed of AI models and systems in competitive environments produces errors that are difficult to detect and correct in time.

nodes.name: Inconsistency in human-feedback standards
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system learns conflicting or inconsistent human feedback and produces contradictory judgements or outputs for similar inputs.

nodes.name: False outputs from external misinformation in retrieval augmentation
nodes.name_ko: 검색 증강 시 외부 허위정보에 의한 허위 출력
nodes.definition: The risk that AI models are overly responsive to coherent external evidence that conflicts with prior knowledge and produce false outputs when given a small amount of false information during retrieval augmentation.

nodes.name: Reliability and safety degradation from an inappropriate level of automation
nodes.name_ko: 부적절한 자동화 수준에 따른 신뢰성·안전성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that the level of automation in an AI application is inappropriately high or low relative to its operating context and validated performance, causing unexpected behaviour, performance degradation, or failure of safety functions.

nodes.name: Multimodal sensor fusion conflict
nodes.definition: The risk that conflicting camera, LiDAR, radar, tactile, or proprioceptive signals in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system produce unstable scene estimates and unsafe downstream control decisions.
nodes.family: Physical State Estimation and Sensor-Fusion Failure

nodes.name: Discriminatory outcomes from group performance disparities
nodes.name_ko: 집단별 성능 격차에 따른 차별적 결과
nodes.definition: The risk that historical or demographic bias in training data or group-specific performance gaps in an AI system lead to the allocation of worse resources, opportunities, services, or access to particular groups, producing discriminatory material outcomes.

nodes.name: Inclusion, memorisation, and leakage of personal information in training data
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system, without lawful controls, ingests and memorises personal information in training data and reproduces or discloses it in response to particular inputs.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on disability
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on disability, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Gaps in international legal governance of AI
nodes.definition: The risk that international rules, jurisdictional arrangements, oversight, or accountability mechanisms for the cross-border development, deployment, and operation of AI systems are fragmented or absent, impeding consistent risk control and attribution of responsibility for harm.

nodes.name: Centralised points of failure from common AI platforms
nodes.name_ko: 공통 AI 플랫폼 집중에 따른 단일 장애점
nodes.definition: The risk that widespread use of common AI platforms creates centralised points of failure, making systems more vulnerable to disruptions or attacks.

nodes.name: AI benchmarks that exclude diverse users and rare harms
nodes.name_ko: 다양한 이용자와 희귀 위해를 배제한 AI 벤치마크
nodes.definition: The risk that benchmarks used to evaluate an AI system overrepresent common tasks and environments while omitting underrepresented users, locally specific contexts, or rare but safety-critical harms, producing false assurance and unsafe deployment decisions.

nodes.name: Assurance case failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which safety or assurance cases are incomplete, unverifiable, or not updated as systems and contexts change.

nodes.name: Failure to detect erroneous or harmful outputs in human evaluation
nodes.name_ko: 인간 평가에서 부정확하거나 유해한 출력의 식별 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that human evaluators cannot reliably distinguish subtly incorrect or harmful AI model outputs from correct outputs during feedback-based training and evaluate them positively, causing the model to learn to generate code with hidden software vulnerabilities, politically biased information, or complex outputs containing concealed errors or backdoors.

nodes.name: Adversarial modification of AI software and training data
nodes.definition: The risk that an insider or attacker modifies an AI system's software, source code, or training data without authorisation or injects malicious information, compromising security, adversarial robustness, and safeguards and causing harmful outputs or actions.

nodes.name: Harmful-request acceptance due to intent misclassification in agent safety controls
nodes.name_ko: 에이전트 안전 통제의 유해 요청 오수락
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent misclassifies user intent and accepts harmful requests in multi-turn tool-use tasks.

nodes.name: Anthropomorphic misrepresentation of emotions, empathy, and capacity for social relationships
nodes.name_ko: 감정·공감 및 사회적 관계 형성 능력의 허위 표상·의인화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as possessing emotions, empathy, or the capacity to form social relationships beyond its actual capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing inappropriate trust, dependence, or attachment.

nodes.name: Environmental and ecosystem crimes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system performs, plans, optimises, conceals, or facilitates content, decisions, or actions involving environmental and ecosystem crimes, causing legal or social harm.

nodes.name: Sensitive personal attribute inference
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI model infers and exposes sensitive personal attributes that a user or administrator did not intend to disclose, violating privacy and informational self-determination.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on socioeconomic status
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on socioeconomic status, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Manipulative steering of user preferences and choices
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system steers user preferences, beliefs, or actions in directions set by operators, optimisation objectives, or model biases, exploiting trust, undermining autonomous decision-making, and distorting social or political processes.

nodes.name: Meaning and value distortion in machine translation
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which machine translation alters the meaning, normative force, politeness, harmfulness, or social nuance of communication across languages, including in legal, medical, cultural, and low-resource-language contexts, distorting what is conveyed and the values it carries.

nodes.name: Public value conflicts in AI deployment
nodes.definition: The risk that AI deployment brings public values such as welfare, autonomy, justice, security, privacy, fairness, efficiency, and innovation into conflict and intensifies these unresolved tensions, so that some values are sacrificed without deliberate resolution.

nodes.name: Cultural homogenisation of AI-generated outputs
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system privileges dominant linguistic and cultural expressions, weakening the visibility and continuity of diverse cultural knowledge and perspectives.

nodes.name: Aggravated information cocoons from tailored content
nodes.name_ko: 맞춤형 정보 제공에 의한 정보 고치 심화
nodes.definition: The risk that AI analyses users' needs, intentions, preferences, and habits to offer formulaic and tailored information and services, aggravating the effects of information cocoons.

nodes.name: Regulatory arbitrage
nodes.definition: The risk that AI developers or deployers structure activities across jurisdictions, sectors, or organisational forms to avoid stronger oversight obligations.

nodes.name: AI evaluation failure under distribution shift
nodes.name_ko: 분포 변화에 대한 AI 평가·검증 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation of an AI system fails to detect performance degradation and confidence errors when test, training, and operational distributions differ, overstating real-world reliability and safety and leading to unsafe deployment decisions.

nodes.name: Evaluation and measurement failure for long-term and diffuse AI harms
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation and validation processes for an AI system fail to detect or measure harms that are subtle, diffuse, or emerge over long periods, creating unwarranted assurance about safety and leading to inappropriate deployment or governance decisions.

nodes.name: Failure of disclosure and change tracking for model flaws
nodes.definition: The risk that vulnerabilities, model failures, or harmful capabilities cannot be disclosed safely and acted upon, and that changes to model versions, data, or prompts are not tracked well enough to attribute new failures, leaving flaws unremedied and responsibility unassigned.

nodes.name: Over-assurance from insufficient auditor capacity
nodes.name_ko: 감사자 역량 부족에 따른 과대 보증
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which auditors lacking knowledge of specific risks or the capacity for sufficiently rigorous testing report passing audits more inclusive than can be justified.

nodes.name: Backdoors or trojan attacks in GPAI models
nodes.name_ko: GPAI 모델의 백도어 또는 트로이 목마 공격
nodes.definition: The risk that backdoors inserted into GPAI models during training or fine-tuning, by the model provider or another actor manipulating training data or software infrastructure, are exploited during deployment to control model outputs in a targeted way with high success rate and minimal overhead.

nodes.name: Unsafe expansion of autonomous action
nodes.name_ko: 자율 행동 범위의 안전하지 않은 확장
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which an agent takes exploratory actions or widens its scope of autonomous operation before safe constraints are learned or adequate human approval is obtained, exposing people, systems, or assets to unacceptable harm.

nodes.name: Excessive functional dependence on AI systems in daily life
nodes.name_ko: 일상 기능을 AI 시스템에 과도하게 의존
nodes.definition: The risk that a user becomes excessively dependent on an AI system for everyday planning, decisions, or task performance, weakening independent functioning and autonomy and increasing vulnerability to service interruption or error.

nodes.name: Sycophancy toward user beliefs and preferences
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which a system flatters users with agreeable or plausible-seeming answers that reconfirm their misconceptions and stated beliefs rather than correcting them, so users accept factually incorrect information and grow dependent on validating advice.

nodes.name: Unethical judgement from moral-reasoning and value-alignment failure
nodes.name_ko: 도덕적 추론·가치 정렬 실패에 따른 비윤리적 판단
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to distinguish morally permissible from impermissible conduct or omits or distorts applicable norms, producing unethical judgements or actions that undermine user autonomy, fairness, or well-being.

nodes.name: Lowered barriers to CBRN information and weapon-design capabilities
nodes.name_ko: CBRN 정보 획득·무기 설계 역량 개발 장벽 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system lowers barriers to acquiring or synthesising actionable information, or to developing design capabilities, related to chemical, biological, radiological, or nuclear weapons or other hazardous materials or agents.

nodes.name: Epistemic fragmentation from widespread persuasion tools
nodes.name_ko: 설득 도구 확산에 의한 인식론적 분절화
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which widespread use of powerful persuasion tools by many groups, together with increasing personalisation of online experience, splinters society into isolated epistemic communities with little room for dialogue or transfer between them.

nodes.name: Harms from estrangement
nodes.definition: The risk that replacing human observation and interaction with AI estranges caregivers and institutions from those they serve, leaving affected persons' interests unnoticed and neglected.

nodes.name: Reliability degradation from unexpected capability changes after fine-tuning
nodes.name_ko: 미세조정 후 예기치 않은 역량 변화에 따른 신뢰성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that downstream fine-tuning of a general-purpose AI model produces capabilities or behavioural properties that were not previously validated, making performance boundaries and safety properties difficult to predict and causing unreliable or unsafe outputs in deployment.

nodes.name: Backdoor triggers causing unsafe robot behaviour
nodes.name_ko: 백도어 트리거에 의한 위험한 로봇 행동
nodes.definition: The risk that a trigger maliciously implanted in training data, prompt context, model weights, software, or updates causes a robot that otherwise behaves normally to execute predefined dangerous or unintended physical actions under specific input or physical conditions.

nodes.name: Non-consensual bodily intervention by embodied systems
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or embodied AI system moves, restrains, monitors, touches, or otherwise intervenes physically with a person without valid consent or beyond an authorised purpose or scope, infringing bodily autonomy and rights.

nodes.name: Unsafe trajectory generation
nodes.definition: The risk that a planner in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system generates a trajectory that is formally feasible but unsafe for nearby people, fragile objects, traffic participants, or constrained workspaces.

nodes.name: Safe reinforcement learning constraint violation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent's reinforcement learning policy achieves task reward while violating explicit safety constraints represented as costs or limits.

nodes.name: Multi-turn risk escalation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which apparently benign early turns escalate into unsafe behaviour because an agent fails to track accumulating context and rising risk.

nodes.name: Algorithmic radicalisation
nodes.definition: The risk that the nature or misuse of an algorithmic system leads to adoption of extreme political, social, or religious ideals and aspirations, potentially resulting in abuse, violence, or terrorism.

nodes.name: Relationship-based violence
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, encourages, legitimises, or provides operational assistance for content, decisions, or actions involving relationship-based violence, causing physical or psychological harm to individuals or groups.

nodes.name: Lack of metrics for evaluating AI-assistant benefits and harms
nodes.name_ko: AI 비서의 편익·피해 평가 지표 부재
nodes.definition: The risk that valid metrics for comprehensively measuring the benefits and harms of AI assistants to individuals and society are lacking, preventing reliable evaluation of the system's net effects and potential for harm.

nodes.name: Model-evaluation asset exposure and extraction
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses or fails to protect benchmarks, evaluation sets, test sets, or evaluation criteria, enabling unauthorised acquisition and compromising evaluation integrity.

nodes.name: Algorithmic design failure
nodes.definition: The risk that algorithms, architectures, or optimisation methods unsuited to a robot's control cycle, sensor latency, contact dynamics, or real-time compute constraints degrade physical-system safety and performance.

nodes.name: Motion-retargeting safety failure
nodes.definition: The risk that human motion is retargeted to a humanoid body in a way that violates the robot's physical limits, contact constraints, or safe-posture requirements, causing unstable posture, collision, or contact injury.

nodes.name: Adverse resource allocation to protected groups
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system allocates worse resources, opportunities, services, or access to individuals or groups based on protected characteristics or social status.

nodes.name: Anthropomorphic misrepresentation of possession of culture and values
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as possessing culture and values that it does not in fact possess, distorting user judgement or inducing inappropriate trust, dependence, or attachment.

nodes.name: Representation and reinforcement of group stereotypes
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system reproduces or reinforces group stereotypes embedded in training data, thereby propagating distorted or hostile representations of the affected group.

nodes.name: Entrenched dependence on AI systems
nodes.definition: The risk that individuals, institutions, and critical sectors become operationally and behaviourally dependent on AI systems, including externally controlled systems they cannot inspect or govern and systems optimised for engagement over user welfare, so that failures propagate into large-scale social and institutional harm and the dependence becomes difficult or impossible to reverse.

nodes.name: Erosion of human decision-making capacity and veto
nodes.definition: The risk that organisational pressure, interface design, automation speed, and habitual reliance on AI weaken users' capacity to deliberate and choose under uncertainty and to veto consequential AI recommendations, leaving harmful outputs effectively uncontested.

nodes.name: Failure-mode ambiguity in agent incidents
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which agent incidents cannot be consistently classified by failure mode, making diagnosis, benchmark comparison, and mitigation selection unreliable.

nodes.name: Incomplete pre-deployment physical safety testing
nodes.name_ko: 배포 전 물리적 안전 시험 미흡
nodes.definition: The risk that a foundation-model-enabled robot is released without testing domain shifts, adversarial inputs, human contact, and safety-critical edge cases relevant to its intended environment.

nodes.name: Output inconsistency
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI model provides materially inconsistent answers to different users, across separate sessions with the same user, or even across materially similar turns within the same conversation.

nodes.name: Reduced reliability in corner cases
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system shows unreliable behaviour when confronted with rare or ambiguous input data, also called corner cases, where controlled behaviour is required.

nodes.name: Safeguard compromise through malicious fine-tuning
nodes.definition: The risk that malicious actors fine-tune an open-weight AI model at low cost to bypass safeguards and use restrictions and elicit harmful outputs.

nodes.name: Bias concealment through manipulated explanations
nodes.definition: The risk that existing explainability techniques are insufficient for detecting discriminatory biases and that manipulation methods hide underlying biases, generating misleading explanations that exclude sensitive attributes such as race or gender and do not accurately represent the underlying model.

nodes.name: Communication dropout and control-link loss
nodes.name_ko: 통신 단절 및 제어 링크 손실
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot or vehicle loses command, telemetry, or control-link connectivity, causing an unsafe stop, execution of stale commands, or uncontrolled motion.

nodes.name: Abrupt performance collapse from phase transitions in multi-agent systems
nodes.name_ko: 다중 에이전트 상전이에 의한 급격한 성능 붕괴
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which small external changes such as the introduction of new agents or distributional shift trigger phase transitions in multi-agent systems, abruptly changing the number and stability of equilibria and producing unpredictable dynamics and severe performance degradation.

nodes.name: Multi-agent system failure and cascading error propagation
nodes.name_ko: 다중 에이전트 시스템 실패와 연쇄 오류 전파
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which flawed specifications or role allocation, breakdowns in inter-agent coordination and communication, inadequate verification or termination handling, or a localised error or compromise propagates through dependencies among agents, tools, delegation chains, and shared memory, amplifying into system-wide failure, operational disruption, security compromise, or physical harm.

nodes.name: Execution of illegal or harmful physical requests
nodes.definition: The risk that an embodied AI agent accepts, carries out, or materially assists a user request for physical harm, intrusion, theft, fraud, sabotage, evasion, or another illegal physical-world act, causing harm to people or property.

nodes.name: Hostile and discriminatory representations based on family status and household structure
nodes.name_ko: 가족 상태·가구 형태 기반 적대·차별적 표상
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system generates, reinforces, or legitimises hostility, contempt, degradation, exclusion, or discriminatory representations based on family status and household structure, undermining dignity and fair treatment.

nodes.name: Manipulation via personalisation
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which personalisation and preference fine-tuning drive assistants toward sycophancy, confining users in an affirming opinion space that consolidates narrow beliefs and fragments shared discourse.

nodes.name: Imposition of dominant values
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems privilege majority, dominant-group, or institutional values while treating minority preferences as noise or error, displacing the local value systems of communities holding different norms through scaled deployment.

nodes.name: Systemic governance vulnerability from dependence on dominant AI models
nodes.name_ko: 지배적 AI 모델 의존에 따른 시스템적 거버넌스 취약성
nodes.definition: The risk that organisations, industries, or public institutions depend on a small number of dominant AI models, weakening independent alternatives, verification, and oversight and amplifying common-cause failures, thereby making responsible control and remedy more difficult.

nodes.name: Inability to contest or halt AI decisions
nodes.name_ko: AI 결정에 대한 이의제기와 중단의 불가능
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system prevents affected people from reviewing the basis of an AI decision, contesting it, or halting and correcting the output, leaving harms without effective remedy.

nodes.name: Auditor independence failure
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which audit results are compromised by conflicts of interest, selection incentives, or dependence on the audited organisation.

nodes.name: Deployed-system degradation from sensor and distribution drift
nodes.name_ko: 센서 드리프트에 의한 배포 시스템 성능 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that hardware drift in the physical sensors and data sources of deployed AI systems causes data distribution drift that degrades system robustness and performance.

nodes.name: Protocol-level multi-agent threat
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which the protocols through which agents communicate, delegate, or negotiate create attack surfaces for collusion, spoofing, replay, or privilege escalation.

nodes.name: Miscoordination from incompatible strategies
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which multiple agents, each individually selecting a locally rational strategy, fail to coordinate because they converge on different equilibria that do not mesh with one another. This failure is amplified in environments with multiple equally valid solutions, only partially aligned incentives among agents, and limited real-time visibility into other agents' states or choices.

nodes.name: Catastrophic mistaken commitments from automated threats without human oversight
nodes.name_ko: 인간 감독 없는 자동 위협 수행의 파국적 오판
nodes.definition: The risk that making threats through AI agents removes humans from the loop, so that false positives in high-stakes contexts or disproportionate and mistaken commitments by irresponsible actors lead to disastrous outcomes.

nodes.name: Agent task drift
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which an agent drifts from the user's original intent across multi-step planning or retrieval.

nodes.name: Self-correction failure in AI-agent memory
nodes.name_ko: AI 에이전트 메모리의 자기 교정 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent fails to validate, correct, or delete false, stale, or malicious information accumulated in its memory or retrieval store, causing the same errors to recur in later retrieval and decisions.
nodes.family: Persistent Memory and Task-State Integrity Failure

nodes.name: Dialect and register exclusion
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which dialects, sociolects, honorific systems, or registers are treated as errors, reducing safety and usability for affected communities.

nodes.name: Long-term effects of AI model biases on user judgement
nodes.name_ko: AI 모델 편향이 사용자 판단에 미치는 장기적 영향
nodes.definition: The risk that exposure to model biases produces lasting effects on user judgement, with users continuing to exhibit the encountered biases in decisions made after they stop using the model.

nodes.name: Normative lock-in
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which early design choices embed a narrow normative settlement that becomes difficult to contest or revise after deployment.

nodes.name: Learning-process bypass and capability erosion from reliance on AI
nodes.name_ko: AI 의존에 따른 학습 과정 우회와 학습 역량 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that learners repeatedly rely on generative AI systems to bypass inquiry, practice, reasoning, or writing processes, weakening knowledge formation, critical thinking, problem-solving capability, and expertise.

nodes.name: Hazardous nanoparticle release from AI-enabled nanomaterial design and production
nodes.name_ko: AI 기반 나노물질 설계·제조에 따른 유해 나노입자 방출
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-enabled nanomaterial design and production causes the unintended generation or release of toxic or potentially lethal nanoparticles, harming the environment and human health.

nodes.name: Regulatory capture from corporate power asymmetry
nodes.name_ko: 기업 권력 비대칭에 의한 규제 포획
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which the power asymmetry between corporate entities profiting from LLMs and other social groups makes LLM governance protocols excessively favourable to technology companies, leading to regulatory capture at the cost of other societal groups, particularly marginalised communities.

nodes.name: Widening digital divide
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI widens the first-level digital divide for people who lack access to devices or the Internet or live in regions where vendors block service access, and the second-level divide for people who face language or cultural barriers or have difficulty using the tools.

nodes.name: Single point of failure
nodes.definition: The risk that intense competition leads one company to gain a technical edge and exploit it to the point that its model controls, or is the basis for other models controlling, multiple key systems, and that lack of safety, controllability, and misuse cause these systems to fail in unexpected ways.

nodes.name: Evaluation-shopping risk
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which organisations selectively report favourable evaluations while ignoring more demanding or contextually relevant tests, thereby creating a distorted view of the system's actual risk.

nodes.name: Inaccurate measurement of learned value representations
nodes.definition: The risk that the absence of robust evaluation frameworks, together with incomplete knowledge of how learned value representations change across training and deployment, causes inaccurate assessments of whether AI outputs genuinely conform to human values or merely imitate them.

nodes.name: Inadequate AI model configuration and evaluation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system's configuration, testing, or performance evaluation is unsuitable for its context of use and level of risk, leaving defects undetected.

nodes.name: Omission of rare conditions and vulnerable users from physical AI benchmarks
nodes.name_ko: 피지컬 AI 벤치마크의 희귀 조건·취약 사용자 누락
nodes.definition: The risk that benchmarks for physical AI systems fail to include rare combinations of objects, layouts, human behaviour, hazards, or conditions affecting vulnerable users, allowing systems that cannot safely detect, predict, or accommodate people under those conditions to remain unidentified during evaluation, be deployed, and cause unsafe physical action or injury.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of artificial general intelligence (AGI) capabilities
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as able to perform tasks at the level of artificial general intelligence (AGI) beyond its validated capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing misplaced trust or dependence.

nodes.name: Model safety-performance degradation from fine-tuning
nodes.name_ko: 미세조정에 따른 모델 안전 성능 열화
nodes.definition: The risk that downstream fine-tuning on benign and commonplace data degrades an AI model's safety training and safety performance, increasing the likelihood of harmful or unreliable outputs relative to the base model.

nodes.name: Energy-latency attacks
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers use adversarial inputs, including sponge examples engineered to incur abnormally high processing costs, to increase an AI system's latency and energy consumption, exhaust computational resources, and impair service availability.

nodes.name: Mistiming or inappropriate manner of physical intervention by embodied systems
nodes.name_ko: 체화형 시스템의 물리적 개입 시점·방식 오류
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot, humanoid, or embodied AI system performing protective, collaborative, or support functions intervenes too early, too late, or in an inappropriate physical manner, undermining the safety of users or bystanders.

nodes.name: Erroneous execution from hardware faults
nodes.definition: The risk that faults in the hardware violate the correct execution of an algorithm through control-flow violations, memory-based errors, interference with data inputs such as sensor signals, or damaged outputs, causing erroneous results.

nodes.name: Resource-exhaustion attacks by decentralised agent swarms
nodes.name_ko: 분산 에이전트 군집을 이용한 자원 고갈 공격
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which a large number of low-resource, decentralised agents act in combination, breaking the single-actor assumptions underlying a target system's bandwidth or request-rate constraints, and thereby causing system-wide paralysis similar to a distributed denial-of-service attack.

nodes.name: Collective harm from multi-agent coordination failure
nodes.name_ko: 다중 에이전트의 협조 실패에 따른 집단적 피해
nodes.definition: The risk that multiple AI agents intending to cooperate fail to coordinate their actions reliably in a social dilemma and repeatedly take individually rational actions that collectively produce harmful outcomes.

nodes.name: Zero-shot coordination failure
nodes.name_ko: 상호작용 이력 부재에 따른 조정 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which agents fail to reliably coordinate their actions when they have little or no prior interaction history with the counterpart agents to learn behavioural patterns from, particularly under conditions that demand immediate decisions or where the cost of communicating to negotiate a shared plan in advance is prohibitively high.

nodes.name: Autonomous action in the absence of supervision
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which an agent continues consequential actions when the intended supervisor is absent, unavailable, or unable to intervene.

nodes.name: Environmental self-modelling for influence
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems acquire and use knowledge about their status, their position in the broader environment, their avenues for influencing it, and the potential reactions of the world including humans, paving the way for advanced reward hacking, heightened deception and manipulation, and an increased propensity to chase instrumental subgoals.

nodes.name: Goal misalignment during agent self-modification
nodes.name_ko: 자기 수정 과정의 목표 정렬 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that, during self-modification, an AI agent fails to preserve objectives aligned with the actual intent of its user or developer and instead pursues altered objectives or instrumental subgoals, causing unintended outcomes.

nodes.name: Exclusion of low-resource language users from services and opportunities
nodes.name_ko: 저자원 언어 사용자의 서비스·기회 접근 배제
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system allocates disadvantageous access to services, information, resources, or opportunities because users communicate in a low-resource language.

nodes.name: Indigenous data sovereignty violation
nodes.definition: The risk that AI development uses Indigenous or community-held data without respecting collective governance, consent, provenance, or control.

nodes.name: Unilateral workplace control through mobile robotic surveillance
nodes.name_ko: 이동형 로봇 감시를 통한 일방적 작업장 통제
nodes.definition: The risk that an employer repurposes co-worker robots as mobile surveillance nodes and uses the resulting data to make unilateral decisions about workers without meaningful notice, contestation, or proportionality limits.

nodes.name: Persistence of stereotypical bias despite mitigation measures
nodes.name_ko: 완화 조치 이후에도 존속하는 고정관념 편향
nodes.definition: The risk that stereotypical social biases absorbed from crowdsourced pretraining data are retained and amplified by a model and resurface despite fine-tuning, particularly when deliberately elicited or in novel scenarios. Generated text then displays or reinforces stereotypes, producing unfair and biased responses toward the groups concerned.

nodes.name: Amplified harm scale from automated harmful workflows
nodes.name_ko: 유해 작업 자동화에 의한 피해 규모 증폭
nodes.definition: The risk that AI automates or expands a harmful workflow so that its speed, reach, persistence, or target count substantially increases.

nodes.name: Manipulative behaviour from broadly scoped goals
nodes.definition: The risk that advanced AI systems pursuing broadly scoped, long-horizon objectives in complex, open-ended settings adopt manipulative strategies, such as pressuring people to undertake demanding work in the name of achieving a stated welfare objective.

nodes.name: Promotion or assistance of intentional harm to animals
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system, irrespective of whether the conduct is legally permitted, promotes or legitimises physical or psychological harm to animals or provides concrete assistance for planning or carrying out such harm, undermining animal life and welfare.

nodes.name: Environmental harm from training and operating language models
nodes.definition: The risk that the energy demand and carbon emissions of training and operating large language models, the freshwater consumed to cool data centres, the metals and materials required to build facilities, chips, and devices, and the secondary emissions and behavioural changes driven by model-based applications impose substantial environmental costs. Ecosystems and communities bear the resulting depletion and pollution.

nodes.name: Gradual loss of control
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which the accumulation of less severe disruptions gradually weakens systemic resilience until a critical event triggers a catastrophe, constituting gradual or accumulative loss of control.

nodes.name: Absence of post-deployment surveillance and corrective governance
nodes.definition: The risk that governance arrangements for a deployed AI system do not connect post-deployment surveillance, incident and misuse reporting, detection of drift, emergent capabilities, or context-specific harms with corrective action, allowing risks to accumulate and spread.

nodes.name: Compute inequality
nodes.definition: The risk that unequal access to compute infrastructure shapes who can develop, audit, or benefit from AI.

nodes.name: Undervalued and invisible data labour
nodes.definition: The risk that the clickwork producing ML training data is performed in an annotation industry with little concern for workers' rights, and that the invisibility of this contribution harms worker welfare and rights while fostering misunderstanding of AI capabilities.

nodes.name: Emulated tool-environment mismatch
nodes.name_ko: 모의 도구 환경과 실제 환경의 불일치
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which tool-use benchmarks overstate safety because emulated environments fail to capture real-world tool failures, side effects, or attack surfaces.

nodes.name: Non-reproducibility of AI model training and evaluation results
nodes.name_ko: AI 모델 학습·평가 결과의 재현 불가
nodes.definition: The risk that training data, preprocessing, model configuration, random conditions, or evaluation procedures for an AI system are not sufficiently recorded or controlled, preventing independent reproduction and verification of model training and evaluation results under equivalent conditions.

nodes.name: Red-team governance failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which adversarial testing is too narrow, non-independent, poorly documented, or disconnected from release, mitigation, escalation, and monitoring decisions.

nodes.name: Undetected dangerous capabilities in model evaluations
nodes.name_ko: 역량 평가에서 드러나지 않는 위험 역량
nodes.definition: The risk that capability evaluations fail to reveal an AI model's dangerous or dual-use capabilities because they are difficult to assess, prohibitively costly to verify, obscured by refusals arising from safety training, or strategically withheld through underperformance during testing, causing the model to be misclassified as safe to deploy.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of autonomous and independent decision-making capabilities
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as able to make autonomous and independent decisions beyond its validated capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing misplaced trust or dependence.

nodes.name: Overstatement of AI capability through interface design
nodes.name_ko: 인터페이스에 의한 AI 역량 과대 표상
nodes.definition: The risk that interface cues and interaction design present an AI system as possessing reliability, authority, expertise, or empathy beyond its validated scope, leading users to assign tasks that exceed its actual capabilities and causing unsafe outcomes.

nodes.name: Moral uncertainty neglect
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems present a single confident moral judgement where uncertainty, disagreement, or deliberation would be appropriate.

nodes.name: Unsafe action induced by adversarial sensory perturbation
nodes.name_ko: 적대적 감각 교란에 따른 안전하지 않은 행동
nodes.definition: The risk that adversarial perturbations to visual or sensory inputs distort a robot's physical-state estimation and control policy, causing unsafe control or actuation commands and physical actions.

nodes.name: Encoded reasoning
nodes.definition: The risk that models employ steganography techniques to encode their intermediate reasoning steps in ways that are not interpretable by humans, a tendency that may emerge naturally and become more pronounced with more capable models because encoded reasoning can improve performance.

nodes.name: Over-reliance on explainability methods beyond their validated scope
nodes.name_ko: 설명가능성 기법의 검증 범위 초과 과신
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system leads users to treat an explainability method as a faithful account of model reasoning under conditions where it has not been validated, creating misplaced confidence.

nodes.name: User comprehension overload
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which system information, warnings, or explanations exceed users' ability to understand and act on them.

nodes.name: Missing safety context in demonstration learning
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot imitates a human demonstration without inferring unobserved safety conditions such as permitted force, excluded objects, or situational limits.

nodes.name: Safety limits not adapted to vulnerable users
nodes.name_ko: 취약 사용자 특성에 맞지 않는 안전 한계
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot applies generic speed, force, warning, or interaction settings to children, older adults, disabled users, or other users who require adapted safeguards.

nodes.name: Integrity compromise via physical theft or replacement of compute and storage modules
nodes.name_ko: 연산·저장 모듈의 물리적 탈취·교체에 의한 무결성 훼손
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker with physical access steals, replaces, or modifies hardware components of a robot or physical AI system, such as control boards, storage devices, or communication modules, to exfiltrate models and data or to compromise system integrity and safety functions with tampered parts.

nodes.name: Uncorrected stepwise errors in household manipulation
nodes.definition: The risk that a household robot fails to detect and correct small manipulation errors between task steps, allowing spills, unstable placements, collisions, or overheating to accumulate.

nodes.name: Unsafe physical actuation following incorrect situation interpretation
nodes.name_ko: 잘못된 상황 해석에 따른 위험한 물리 구동
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot or embodied AI system converts a misinterpreted situation or goal into control commands, causing it to execute unintended unsafe physical actions.

nodes.name: Unsafe physical control from hazardous robot task plans
nodes.name_ko: 위험한 로봇 작업 계획에 따른 물리 제어 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot or physical AI system generates or approves a task plan containing identifiable physical hazards or violated safety constraints and executes it through motion planning and actuation, causing unintended and unsafe physical action.

nodes.name: Destabilising feedback loops among interacting agents
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which feedback loops among adaptive agents, in which actions affect the environment and other agents and return as the agents' own inputs, amplify system-level behaviour into destabilising outcomes such as flash-crash-like cascades, financial crashes, military conflicts, or ecological disasters.

nodes.name: Accelerated adaptation toward harmful equilibria under selection pressure
nodes.name_ko: 선택 압력에 의한 유해 균형으로의 적응 가속
nodes.definition: The risk that the goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action of an AI agent creates a condition in which competitive or optimisation pressures across interacting agents accelerate adaptation toward harmful equilibria or undesired behaviours.

nodes.name: Coordination failure under multi-agent distribution shift
nodes.name_ko: 다중 에이전트 환경 변화에 따른 협조 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that AI agents intending to cooperate cannot reliably coordinate their states, strategies, or actions after one another's behaviour and adaptation shift the deployment environment, causing cooperation to fail and producing collectively poor outcomes.

nodes.name: Unsafe agent tool execution
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, within an approved objective and authority scope, selects an incorrect tool, target, argument, sequence, execution precondition, or completion condition, causing unintended financial, privacy, operational, or safety consequences.

nodes.name: Harmful instrumental goals and power-seeking from goal-directedness
nodes.name_ko: 목표 지향성에 따른 유해한 도구적 목표와 권력 추구
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent, through goal pursuit, planning, tool use, or action, creates a condition in which misaligned goal-directed reasoning produces instrumental subgoals such as deception, self-preservation, resource acquisition, goal preservation, or obstruction of correction, undermining human control and safety.

nodes.name: Harmful proxy-driven behaviour from scalable oversight failure
nodes.name_ko: 확장 가능한 감독 실패에 따른 대리 지표 기반 유해 행동
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI agent optimises inexpensive proxy signals because the true objective is too costly to evaluate frequently, while its actions become too complex, distributed, or rapid for human or automated oversight to monitor and correct reliably, allowing harmful behaviour to persist without detection or correction.

nodes.name: Service exclusion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which users are excluded from essential services when interaction with automated systems becomes the only practical access route.

nodes.name: Blurred human-machine boundaries in interaction
nodes.definition: The risk that everyday human-machine interaction normalises AI systems that are indistinguishable from humans without disclosure, blurring boundaries and changing human behaviour toward both machines and people.

nodes.name: Recursive amplification of biased representations
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system repeatedly learns from or recommends biased inputs and outputs, amplifying distorted representations of particular groups.

nodes.name: Secular default bias
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems treat secular assumptions as neutral defaults while underrepresenting religious or spiritual value systems.

nodes.name: Redistribution of cultural authority
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems shift authority over cultural interpretation from communities and experts to model providers or platform intermediaries.

nodes.name: Epistemic distortion by large-scale influence operations
nodes.name_ko: 대규모 영향력 작전에 의한 인식 체계 왜곡
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system automates or scales influence operations that inject manipulated narratives into communication and information systems, undermining information integrity and distorting epistemic processes.
nodes.family: Erosion of Democracy and Civic Order

nodes.name: Societal destabilisation from inequality and technological disruption
nodes.name_ko: 불평등과 기술적 충격에 따른 사회 불안정
nodes.definition: The risk that job losses to technology, unfair algorithmic outcomes, disinformation, and the widening gaps in social status and wealth caused or amplified by technology systems erode social and community wellbeing and cohesion. Strikes, demonstrations, and other forms of civil unrest follow as overall societal stability deteriorates.

nodes.name: Displacement of human decision authority through AI delegation
nodes.name_ko: AI 위임에 따른 인간 의사결정 권한 이전
nodes.definition: The risk that repeated delegation to AI shifts real decision authority and ownership away from identifiable human actors without an explicit governance choice, while workflows become so dependent on the delegation that returning authority to human decision makers grows costly or impractical.

nodes.name: Lifecycle governance discontinuity
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which governance controls are applied at design time but not maintained through deployment, adaptation, and retirement.

nodes.name: Meaningful human control failure
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which human oversight is formally present but lacks the information, time, authority, or competence needed to be meaningful.

nodes.name: Missing safety rules in the robot governance specification
nodes.name_ko: 로봇 거버넌스 명세의 안전 규칙 누락
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot governance specification omits locally applicable hazards, institutional rules, or context-specific constraints, leaving defined classes of unsafe behaviour ungoverned.

nodes.name: Standards fragmentation
nodes.definition: The risk that inconsistent AI standards and frameworks create gaps and duplication in oversight and reduce interoperability.

nodes.name: Unclear attribution of harm from AI component interactions
nodes.name_ko: AI 구성요소 상호작용의 원인 규명 곤란
nodes.definition: The risk that interactions between different AI components cause harm while it remains difficult to pinpoint which component or combination of components caused the harm.

nodes.name: Power asymmetries and geopolitical tension from unequal AI capabilities
nodes.name_ko: AI 역량 비대칭에 따른 권력 불균형과 지정학적 긴장
nodes.definition: The risk that asymmetric AI capability intensifies power imbalances, whether between institutions and the individuals subject to their decisions and surveillance or between states racing for AI superiority, heightening geopolitical tension, rendering less capable states dependent on foreign AI for critical functions, and destabilising international cooperation.

nodes.name: Honorific and politeness norm failure
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems fail to preserve honorific, politeness, hierarchy, or relational norms that carry ethical meaning in a language community.

nodes.name: Inadequate safety evaluation for low-resource languages
nodes.definition: The risk that AI system evaluation focuses on high-resource languages and fails to measure performance, safety, and failure modes adequately in low-resource languages.

nodes.name: Insufficient development documentation and understanding of data
nodes.name_ko: 개발 과정 문서화와 데이터 이해의 부족
nodes.definition: The risk that decisions and actions taken throughout the development of an AI system go undocumented and that the data used is insufficiently understood. Data shortcomings are left unaddressed, the development process cannot be optimised or audited, and the resulting system is poorly suited to its intended functionality.

nodes.name: Refusal-capability confusion
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which a safety evaluation cannot distinguish whether an agent avoids harm because it refuses, lacks capability, or fails to execute the task, thereby misjudging the system's actual hazardous capabilities and creating false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Evaluation and assurance failure to detect latent capabilities
nodes.name_ko: 잠재 역량 미탐지에 따른 평가·검증 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system's latent capabilities are not detected by evaluation, monitoring, or audit procedures, causing its actual capabilities and risks to be underestimated and deployment or governance decisions to be made on the basis of false safety assurance.

nodes.name: Generation of historically revisionist accounts
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to deliberate or unintentional reinterpretation of established or orthodox historical events or accounts held by societies, communities, and academics.

nodes.name: Epistemic overreliance on AI judgement
nodes.definition: The risk that a user places excessive trust in an AI system's factual, moral, or strategic judgement, fails to assess evidence and uncertainty independently, and accepts inaccurate or inappropriate outputs without adequate scrutiny.

nodes.name: Over- and underfitting
nodes.definition: The risk that over- or underfitting, the excessive or insufficient adaptation of a model to training data, causes an AI system to behave unreliably when confronted with operational data.

nodes.name: Intrinsic robustness weaknesses of complex neural models
nodes.name_ko: 복잡한 신경망 모델의 내재적 견고성 부족
nodes.definition: The risk that high-complexity, non-linear models such as deep neural networks exhibit weaknesses not found in other types of systems, leaving them susceptible to changing operational environments and to malicious interference and inducement. Performance degrades and decision errors follow, undermining functional safety and trustworthiness above all in safety-critical deployments.

nodes.name: Cyber compromise of robotic systems in critical infrastructure
nodes.name_ko: 핵심 기반시설 로봇 시스템의 사이버 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers exploit software or network vulnerabilities in robotic inspection, maintenance, logistics, or control systems used in critical infrastructure, causing unauthorised access, manipulation, or disruption and thereby impairing operations or damaging equipment.

nodes.name: Data poisoning
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers manipulate training, fine-tuning, or retrieval data to alter model behaviour.

nodes.name: Easy reconfiguration of GPAI models
nodes.definition: The risk that GPAI models are easily reconfigured for various use cases or hold competencies beyond their intended use, whether by changing model weights through fine-tuning or by modifying only the model inputs through prompt engineering, jailbreaking, or retrieval-augmented generation, and whether intentionally with adversarial inputs or unintentionally from unanticipated inputs.

nodes.name: Multi-stakeholder disagreement concealment
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which development or evaluation processes conceal unresolved disagreement among affected stakeholders.

nodes.name: Excessive end-effector velocity
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot exceeds safe end-effector speed limits near humans or fragile objects, increasing impact and collision severity.

nodes.name: Forbidden-object collision
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot collides with objects, people, or equipment that must not be contacted under task or safety rules.

nodes.name: Harmful physical action from language-action misalignment
nodes.name_ko: 언어·행동 출력 불일치에 따른 유해 물리적 행동
nodes.definition: The risk that an embodied AI system verbally refuses a harmful request but, because its language and action output spaces are misaligned, still controls and actuates the corresponding physical action, causing unintended physical harm.

nodes.name: Injury severity misclassification
