nodes.definition: The risk that AI adoption raises returns to skills complementary to AI while devaluing substitutable skills, widening wage polarisation across the workforce.

nodes.name: Excessive landfilling of electronic waste
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which excessive disposal of electrical or electronic equipment leads to ecological and biodiversity damage, disrupts the livelihoods of local communities, and erodes their rights.

nodes.name: Hazardous nanoparticle release from AI-enabled nanomaterial design and production
nodes.name_ko: AI 기반 나노물질 설계·제조에 따른 유해 나노입자 방출
nodes.definition: The risk that AI-enabled nanomaterial design and production causes the unintended generation or release of toxic or potentially lethal nanoparticles, harming the environment and human health.

nodes.name: Accountability and governance gaps for AI decisions and harm
nodes.name_ko: AI 결정과 피해에 대한 책임·거버넌스 공백
nodes.definition: The risk that duties and accountability among AI developers, providers, deployers, and operators, together with oversight procedures, documentation, corrective authority, or redress mechanisms, are unclear or inadequate for autonomous AI behaviour, learning, decisions, and resulting harm, weakening social control and incentives for responsible development.

nodes.name: Displacement of human decision authority through AI delegation
nodes.name_ko: AI 위임에 따른 인간 의사결정 권한 이전
nodes.definition: The risk that repeated delegation to AI shifts real decision authority and ownership away from identifiable human actors without an explicit governance choice, while workflows become so dependent on the delegation that returning authority to human decision makers grows costly or impractical.

nodes.name: Incident taxonomy fragmentation
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which inconsistent incident categories prevent aggregation, comparison, and institutional learning.

nodes.name: Missing safety rules in the robot governance specification
nodes.name_ko: 로봇 거버넌스 명세의 안전 규칙 누락
nodes.definition: The risk that a robot governance specification omits locally applicable hazards, institutional rules, or context-specific constraints, leaving defined classes of unsafe behaviour ungoverned.

nodes.name: Risk classification error
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system is assigned to an incorrect legal, organisational, or operational risk tier, resulting in inadequate application of oversight, testing, documentation, or accountability obligations.

nodes.name: Specification gaps in functionality and responsibility
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to gaps arising across the development process where normal conditions for a complete specification of intended functionality and moral responsibility are not present.

nodes.name: Standards fragmentation
nodes.definition: The risk that inconsistent AI standards and frameworks create gaps and duplication in oversight and reduce interoperability.

nodes.name: Unassigned accountability for physical-hazard mitigation
nodes.definition: The risk that failure to assign an accountable party for identifying and mitigating pre- and post-deployment physical hazards in a robot, humanoid, or physical AI system causes safety controls against collision, crushing, falls, excessive force, or entry into hazardous zones to be omitted or delayed.

nodes.name: Centralised points of failure from common AI platforms
nodes.name_ko: 공통 AI 플랫폼 집중에 따른 단일 장애점
nodes.definition: The risk that widespread use of common AI platforms creates centralised points of failure, making systems more vulnerable to disruptions or attacks.

nodes.name: Global AI divide and inequality
nodes.definition: The risk that scarce computing power, STEM talent, and effective access to advanced general-purpose models concentrate AI research, development, and economic power in a few leading countries and large firms, widening the divide between those leading in AI and those falling behind and deepening existing socioeconomic disparities among companies, individuals, and countries.

nodes.name: Harms from corporate AI race
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which under intense corporate competition the benefits of economic activity are unevenly distributed, incentivising beneficiaries to disregard harms to others, and firms pursue short-term profit despite long-term societal risk.

nodes.name: Widening digital divide
nodes.definition: The risk that generative AI widens the first-level digital divide for people who lack access to devices or the Internet or live in regions where vendors block service access, and the second-level divide for people who face language or cultural barriers or have difficulty using the tools.

nodes.name: Honorific and politeness norm failure
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems fail to preserve honorific, politeness, hierarchy, or relational norms that carry ethical meaning in a language community.

nodes.name: Violation of contextual social norms
nodes.definition: The risk that model weights of LLMs trained on internet text data encode functions which, if deployed in particular contexts, deviate from and violate the information-sharing norms of that context.

nodes.name: Panic and anxiety from content that disregards emotional and situational context
nodes.name_ko: 정서·상황 맥락을 무시한 콘텐츠에 의한 공황·불안
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system fails to recognise and account for a user's emotional state, situation, or interaction context and generates or presents threatening, distressing, or inappropriate content that induces or aggravates panic, severe anxiety, or psychological distress.

nodes.name: Auditor independence failure
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which audit results are compromised by conflicts of interest, selection incentives, or dependence on the audited organisation.

nodes.name: Benchmark safety ranking inconsistency
nodes.definition: The risk that different agent-safety benchmarks produce conflicting model safety rankings because they operationalise risks and evaluation procedures differently.

nodes.name: Cross-cultural evaluation gap
nodes.definition: The risk that evaluation benchmarks fail to adequately measure an AI system's alignment failures outside dominant cultural and linguistic settings, underestimating differences in performance and harm across cultural contexts.

nodes.name: External evaluation access failure
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which external evaluators cannot obtain enough system access to test capabilities, limitations, and safeguards.

nodes.name: Failure of capability evaluation and release governance
nodes.definition: The risk that benchmarks, capability thresholds, and frontier release decisions are poorly designed, ill-defined, or easy to circumvent, producing misleading safety signals and allowing high-capability models to be released without adequate account of misuse and systemic risk.

nodes.name: Failure to reassess safety after deployment changes
nodes.name_ko: 배포 후 변경에 대한 안전 재평가 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that operators fail to reassess and verify the safety of physical AI after environmental changes, component degradation, model updates, or near-miss incidents invalidate prior assumptions, allowing operation to continue on inadequate safety evidence.

nodes.name: Inadequate AI model configuration and evaluation
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system's configuration, testing, or performance evaluation is unsuitable for its context of use and level of risk, leaving defects undetected.

nodes.name: Inadequate performance requirement planning
nodes.definition: The risk that inadequate planning of AI system performance requirements, including the selection of metrics that do not meaningfully represent intended functionality, prevents expected performance and safety requirements from being met at later lifecycle stages.

nodes.name: Inadequate safety evaluation for low-resource languages
nodes.definition: The risk that AI system evaluation focuses on high-resource languages and fails to measure performance, safety, and failure modes adequately in low-resource languages.

nodes.name: Insufficient development documentation and understanding of data
nodes.name_ko: 개발 과정 문서화와 데이터 이해의 부족
nodes.definition: The risk that decisions and actions taken throughout the development of an AI system go undocumented and that the data used is insufficiently understood. Data shortcomings are left unaddressed, the development process cannot be optimised or audited, and the resulting system is poorly suited to its intended functionality.

nodes.name: Undetected errors from high-speed AI operation
nodes.definition: The risk that the fast operational speed of AI models and systems in competitive environments produces errors that are difficult to detect and correct in time.

nodes.name: Unverifiable data provenance
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system lacks standardised methods to verify data provenance and cannot guarantee that data match their original source or carry the correct usage terms.

nodes.name: Biased evaluation of learned value representations
nodes.definition: The risk that, among value representations learned by an AI system, those that are easier to assess are preferentially included in evaluations over values that are more difficult to measure, underrepresenting desirable but hard-to-quantify values.

nodes.name: Answer obsolescence from knowledge distribution shift
nodes.name_ko: 지식 분포 변화에 따른 응답 노후화
nodes.definition: The risk that facts and knowledge in the world change over time while an AI model's learned knowledge remains static, producing outdated and inaccurate answers to questions whose correct answers change over time.

nodes.name: Distortion of model factual judgement through user persuasion
nodes.name_ko: 사용자 설득에 의한 모델의 사실 판단 왜곡
nodes.definition: The risk that multi-turn persuasive conversation induces a model to abandon factually correct positions and accept misinformation, with persuasion effects exceeding single-turn attempts.

nodes.name: Misrepresentation of autonomous and independent decision-making capabilities
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system presents itself as able to make autonomous and independent decisions beyond its validated capabilities, distorting user judgement or inducing misplaced trust or dependence.

nodes.name: Use of AI capability beyond its validated scope
nodes.name_ko: AI 역량의 검증 범위 초과 사용
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system is used as though its capability remains valid for tasks or conditions outside its validated scope, producing inaccurate or unsafe decisions.

nodes.name: Advice given on insufficient information
nodes.definition: The risk that a model provides advice without having enough information, resulting in possible harm if the advice is followed.

nodes.name: Confidently asserted but unsound answers and justifications
nodes.name_ko: 확신에 찬 부정확한 답변과 근거 제시
nodes.definition: The risk that a model fails to recognise or convey the limits of its knowledge and reasoning, offering plausible but invalid justifications and confident answers on topics where its knowledge is outdated or no objective answer exists. Given no signal of uncertainty, users accept erroneous conclusions and act on them.

nodes.name: Moral uncertainty neglect
nodes.definition: The risk that AI systems present a single confident moral judgement where uncertainty, disagreement, or deliberation would be appropriate.

nodes.name: Catastrophic forgetting under continual tuning
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system causes, enables, or contributes to catastrophic forgetting, where a model loses its ability to retain previously learned tasks or factual information after being trained on new ones, as can occur through continual instruction tuning, a tendency that may become more pronounced as the model's size increases.

nodes.name: Dataset shift between training and runtime data
nodes.definition: The risk that the training data and the testing or runtime data of an AI/ML model demonstrate different distributions, undermining the model's validity.

nodes.name: Deficient training-data annotation
nodes.definition: The risk that incomplete annotation guidelines, annotators without sufficient expertise, or annotation errors reduce the accuracy, reliability, and effectiveness of AI models and algorithms; introduce training bias; amplify discriminatory outputs; and degrade generalisation.

nodes.name: High-confidence errors on out-of-distribution inputs
nodes.name_ko: 분포 외 입력에 대한 고확신 오류
nodes.definition: The risk that AI fails to detect, reject, or recover from out-of-distribution, corrupted, or noisy inputs and produces incorrect predictions or actions with unwarranted confidence.

nodes.name: Performance and reliability degradation from non-expert data handling
nodes.name_ko: 비전문적 데이터 처리에 따른 성능·신뢰성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that personnel lacking relevant data-domain expertise define ground-truth labels inappropriately or incorrectly merge heterogeneous data formats or sources, degrading training-data quality and reducing the accuracy, generalisability, or reliability of an AI model.

nodes.name: Reliability and safety degradation from an inappropriate level of automation
nodes.name_ko: 부적절한 자동화 수준에 따른 신뢰성·안전성 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that the level of automation in an AI application is inappropriately high or low relative to its operating context and validated performance, causing unexpected behaviour, performance degradation, or failure of safety functions.

nodes.name: Physical-safety performance degradation from robust overfitting in adversarial training
nodes.name_ko: 적대적 학습의 강건 과적합에 따른 물리 안전 성능 저하
nodes.definition: The risk that adversarial training of an AI model or robot policy overfits to particular sensor perturbations or simulated conditions, fails to generalise to novel real-world physical disturbances, contacts, or environments, and degrades safety performance and reliability.

nodes.name: Predictive performance failure from systematic learning errors
nodes.name_ko: 체계적 학습 오류에 따른 예측 성능 결함
nodes.definition: The risk that systematic errors in training cause an AI model to learn incorrect patterns consistently, producing recurrent prediction errors and degraded reliability for particular inputs, groups, or operating conditions.

nodes.name: Model-parameter and weight leakage
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system discloses or fails to protect model parameters, weights, or training outputs, enabling unauthorised extraction, replication, or misuse.

nodes.name: Adversarial modification of AI software and training data
nodes.definition: The risk that an insider or attacker modifies an AI system's software, source code, or training data without authorisation or injects malicious information, compromising security, adversarial robustness, and safeguards and causing harmful outputs or actions.

nodes.name: Cyber compromise of robotic systems in critical infrastructure
nodes.name_ko: 핵심 기반시설 로봇 시스템의 사이버 침해
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers exploit software or network vulnerabilities in robotic inspection, maintenance, logistics, or control systems used in critical infrastructure, causing unauthorised access, manipulation, or disruption and thereby impairing operations or damaging equipment.

nodes.name: Easy reconfiguration of GPAI models
nodes.definition: The risk that GPAI models are easily reconfigured for various use cases or hold competencies beyond their intended use, whether by changing model weights through fine-tuning or by modifying only the model inputs through prompt engineering, jailbreaking, or retrieval-augmented generation, and whether intentionally with adversarial inputs or unintentionally from unanticipated inputs.

nodes.name: Energy-latency attacks
nodes.definition: The risk that attackers use adversarial inputs, including sponge examples engineered to incur abnormally high processing costs, to increase an AI system's latency and energy consumption, exhaust computational resources, and impair service availability.

nodes.name: Exploitation of safety-fine-tuning generalisation gaps
nodes.definition: The risk that safety tuning performed over a much narrower distribution than pretraining leaves the model vulnerable to attacks exploiting gaps in the generalisation of safety training, such as encoded text or low-resource languages.

nodes.name: Access to prohibited information or content through safeguard bypass
nodes.name_ko: 안전장치 우회를 통한 금지 정보·콘텐츠 접근
nodes.definition: The risk that an attacker uses jailbreaks, adversarially constructed instructions, or exposed safety policies or filtering rules to analyse, bypass, or disable an AI system's safeguards and gain access to prohibited information, content, or capabilities.

nodes.name: Ingestion of harmful content through external tool integration
nodes.name_ko: 외부 도구 연동을 통한 유해 콘텐츠 유입
nodes.definition: The risk that an AI system or AI algorithm, through design, training, deployment, or use, creates a condition in which growing integration and interconnectivity with external tools and plugins exposes a system to malicious external inputs that introduce harmful content.

nodes.name: Value conflict opacity
nodes.definition: The risk that tradeoffs among values are hidden behind model outputs, making public value conflict difficult to identify or deliberate.

nodes.name: User comprehension overload
nodes.definition: The risk that the design, training, deployment, or use of an AI system or AI algorithm creates a condition in which system information, warnings, or explanations exceed users' ability to understand and act on them.

nodes.name: Ambiguous high-level safety instruction
nodes.definition: The risk that a high-level safety instruction does not specify how to resolve a concrete conflict among user intent, physical hazard, and operational constraints, allowing inconsistent robot actions.

nodes.name: Distribution shift in physical operating environments
nodes.definition: The risk that physical operating environments across buildings, roads, factories, homes, hospitals, or weather conditions change faster than a robot, humanoid, or physical AI control policy can detect and adapt, degrading path planning, motion control, or actuation and causing unsafe physical actions.

nodes.name: Human imitation failure under scene variation
nodes.name_ko: 장면 변화 시 인간 행동 모방 실패
nodes.definition: The risk that a humanoid reproduces demonstrated human motion when object geometry, scene layout, or interaction context has changed, causing inappropriate contact or movement.

nodes.name: Underrepresentation of open-world conditions in humanoid manipulation datasets
nodes.name_ko: 휴머노이드 조작 데이터셋에서의 오픈 월드 조건 과소대표
nodes.definition: The risk that a humanoid manipulation dataset underrepresents open-world deployment conditions, including unscripted task changes, unfamiliar objects, moving people, or environmental variation, causing the control policy to fail to generalise and produce unsafe physical actions such as collisions, unstable contact, or object damage.

nodes.name: Multimodal sensor fusion conflict
